selection_rationale: Poland is a major remaining gap in the European country layer. Its role in EU manufacturing, eastern-flank security, SAFE financing, renewable expansion, first nuclear project and demographic transition makes it a high-value structural context for existing Russia, France and regional macro research.
contrary_evidence: Poland's rapid growth, strong manufacturing integration, improving infrastructure and large EU investment flows argue against treating demographic decline or coal dependence as immediate evidence of structural stagnation.

High defence spending and strategic investment do not automatically create domestic productive capacity; imported equipment, inflation, labour scarcity and execution bottlenecks can reduce the growth return.
limitations: September 2026 CPI is a flash estimate and may be revised in the full release.
Defence-spending and SAFE domestic-content statements use government programme definitions and do not measure realized local value added.
Migration statistics are more uncertain than resident-population estimates because temporary and refugee populations can change quickly.
Nuclear capacity discussed is planned and under licensing/construction preparation; it is not operating generation.

en.title: Poland: convergence, security-state investment and the transition from coal-intensive growth to a higher-capital economy
en.deck: Poland combines fast convergence, manufacturing integration and EU-funded investment with demographic contraction, renewed inflation, record defence spending and a rapid renewable-nuclear energy transition.
en.regime: Investment-intensive convergence under security pressure: strong growth and EU capital inflows coexist with demographic contraction, inflation sensitivity, record defence commitments and a transition away from coal-heavy electricity.
en.key_risk: Security, social and energy-investment commitments expand faster than labour supply and productivity, keeping inflation and financing costs high while raising long-run fiscal pressure.
watch: Productivity response to EU and defence investment
Renewable grid integration and nuclear licensing/construction
Trade balance and exposure to German industrial demand

pt-BR.title: Polônia: convergência, investimento do Estado de segurança e a transição de um crescimento intensivo em carvão para uma economia mais capitalizada
pt-BR.deck: A Polônia combina convergência rápida, integração manufatureira e investimento financiado pela UE com contração demográfica, nova inflação, gasto recorde em defesa e rápida transição energética renovável-nuclear.
pt-BR.regime: Convergência intensiva em investimento sob pressão de segurança: crescimento forte e capital europeu coexistem com contração demográfica, sensibilidade inflacionária, compromissos recordes de defesa e transição da eletricidade intensiva em carvão.
pt-BR.key_risk: Compromissos de segurança, sociais e energéticos crescem mais rápido que oferta de trabalho e produtividade, mantendo inflação e custos financeiros altos e elevando pressão fiscal de longo prazo.
